stanzas: ほたるのひかり。まどのゆき。
書（ふみ）よむつき日。かさねつゝ。
いつしか年も。すぎのとを。
あけてぞけさは。わかれゆく。
とまるもゆくも。かぎりとて。
かたみにおもふちよろづの。
こゝろのはしを。ひとことに。
さきくとばかり。うたふなり。
つくしのきはみ。みちのおく。
うみやまとほく。へだつとも。
そのまごころは。へだてなく。
ひとつにつくせ。くにのため。
千島（ちしま）のおくも。おきなはも。
やしまのうちの。まもりなり。
いたらんくにに。いさをしく。
つとめよわがせ。つつがなく。
orig.credit: Inagaki Chikai; Shōgaku shōka-shū, first volume (1881)

stanzas: The light of the fireflies, the snow at the window:
the days and months of reading books we have piled up,
and before we knew it the years too have passed; the cedar door
we open, and this morning we part and go.
Those who stay and those who go, at this the end,
the ten thousand thousand things each thinks for the other,
the edge of our hearts, in a single word,
only 'be well!' is what we sing.
The far end of Tsukushi, the depths of Michinoku,
though sea and mountain lie far between us,
that true heart, with nothing between,
give it whole, as one, for the country.
The far reaches of Chishima, and Okinawa too,
are the guard of what lies within the Eight Islands.
In the land you go to, valiantly
do your duty, my dear one, and come to no harm.
Hotaru no hikari, mado no yuki,
fumi yomu tsukihi, kasanetsutsu,
itsushika toshi mo, sugi no to o
akete zo kesa wa, wakare yuku.
Tomaru mo yuku mo, kagiri tote,
katami ni omou chiyorozu no
kokoro no hashi o, hitokoto ni,
sakiku to bakari, utau nari.
Tsukushi no kiwami, Michi no oku,
umi yama tōku, hedatsu tomo,
sono magokoro wa, hedate naku,
hitotsu ni tsukuse, kuni no tame.
Chishima no oku mo, Okinawa mo,
Yashima no uchi no, mamori nari.
Itaran kuni ni, isaoshiku
tsutomeyo waga se, tsutsuga naku.

notes: Romanization: modified Hepburn of the words as they are read and sung; the historical kana spelling of the original is not transliterated letter by letter (おもふ omou, うたふ utau, きはみ kiwami, とほく tōku, おきなは Okinawa, いさをしく isaoshiku). If the editor wants the written kana transliterated instead, these are the forms to change: omofu, utafu, kihami, tohoku, Okinaha, isawoshiku.

The original separates phrases with 。; the romanization gives them as commas inside a line and a full stop where the sense ends. Glosses in brackets in the original (書（ふみ）, 千島（ちしま）) are readings and are romanized once (fumi, Chishima); ゝ (repeat sign) is written out (kasanetsutsu, kokoro).
line 1.1: fireflies and window snow allude to the Chinese story of two poor scholars who read by the light of fireflies and by the light of snow; the line names the images only, as the original does.

lines 1.3-1.4: 'sugi' is a pivot word: 'passing' (the years have passed) and 'cedar' (sugi no to, 'the cedar door'); 'akete' is both 'opening' the door and the day or year breaking. The translation keeps the door; the double sense cannot be kept in English.
line 2.2: 'katami ni' = 'mutually, each for the other'; 'chiyorozu' (a thousand times ten thousand) = countless.
line 2.4: 'sakiku' = 'safely, in good fortune' (an archaic farewell word), given as 'be well!'.
line 3.1: Tsukushi = the old name of Kyushu (the far south-west); Michi no oku (Michinoku) = the far north of Honshu. Kept as names.

line 4.1: Chishima = the Kuril Islands; Okinawa = the Ryukyus: the northern and southern limits of the realm in 1881. This stanza was rewritten in later printings as the borders changed; the text here is the 1881 one.
line 4.2: Yashima, 'the Eight Islands', an old name for Japan.
line 4.4: 'waga se', 'my se': an old word a woman uses for her husband or brother (or a beloved man); rendered 'my dear one'. The stanza reads as a farewell to a man going to guard the frontier.
